summary: Caleb Sargeant's personal site and CV (calebsargeant.com, apex-canonical). data/*.yml is the single source of truth; scripts/build.py renders it with Jinja2 into dist/, which ships as Cloudflare Workers static assets. The same data renders three A4 print sheets that Playwright prints to the CV, JDs & Duties and cover-letter PDFs, plus the files for assistants: a markdown twin of every page, llms.txt, llms-full.txt, and the MCP search corpus (.docs-index/index/website.json) that CI puts in R2. No framework, no bundler: one site stylesheet, one print stylesheet, progressive-enhancement JS only.

data.purpose: THE source of truth. Every fact about Caleb is written here once and nowhere else; the site and all three PDFs are renderings of these five files. Never edit a rendered page or a PDF.

files.data/profile.yml: The person: name, headline, tagline, location, contact, links, summary, the cover-letter paragraphs, the home-page stats and the availability banner.
files.data/experience.yml: Every role, newest sorted at build time: id, company, title, dates (YYYY-MM or `present`), focus tags, summary, stack chips, highlights (CV) and grouped duties (JDs PDF). `duties_see` borrows another role's duty list.
files.data/education.yml: Certifications, qualifications and schooling, plus `in_progress`. `featured: true` selects the CV's short education list.
files.data/courses.yml: Courses and training with institution, date and duration. `featured: true` selects the CV's course shortlist.
files.data/skills.yml: Grouped technical skills with a 1 to 5 level and optional years, plus soft skills. `cv: true` selects the CV's HIGHLIGHTS block.

templates.purpose: Jinja templates, rendered with StrictUndefined so a typo fails the build. Site pages extend base.html and override blocks; the print sheets are standalone documents that link only assets/print.css. templates/md/ is markdown, rendered by a second environment with autoescape off: the page twins, llms.txt, llms-full.txt and the MCP corpus, all sharing md/_macros.md. Layout only, never content.

files.templates/base.html: Owns doctype, head, the pre-paint theme bootstrap, the sticky nav built from `nav`, the footer, the command-palette markup and the script tags. Derives title and meta description from `page`, so a child never sets them, and links the markdown twin (rel=alternate type=text/markdown) when page.markdown is set.
files.templates/home.html: Home: hero with the #hero-net canvas, availability, stats, skill matrix, current roles, links out.
files.templates/experience.html: The timeline: every role as a .tl-card, with the full duty list inside a keyboard-operable <details>.
files.templates/education.html: Certifications, qualifications, what is in progress, and the course list.
files.templates/cv.html: The CV on screen, with the focus filter toolbar and a link to the PDF.
files.templates/contact.html: Email, phone, LinkedIn, GitHub, docs and the booking link.
files.templates/404.html: Not-found page, served with a real 404 by the Worker.
files.templates/print/cv.html: A4 CV sheet, two columns, budgeted at 1 to 2 pages. Printed to Caleb_Sargeant_CV.pdf.
files.templates/print/jds.html: A4 job-descriptions sheet: contents page plus every role's full duty list. Grows with the data by design.
files.templates/print/cover.html: A4 cover letter from profile.yml's cover_letter block. One page.
files.templates/social/og.html: The 1200x630 Open Graph card. Rendered to a committed PNG by scripts/render_images.py, not part of the site build.
files.templates/md/_macros.md: Shared markdown fragments (role_line, role_detail, role_facts, education_entry/line, course_line, skill_group, stats, contact_direct, profile_links, documents), imported with context. Labels go through t().
files.templates/md/home.md: Markdown twins of the five sitemap pages (home, experience, education, cv, contact), one template per page, rendered with the same context as the HTML into <path>index.md in every locale.
files.templates/md/llms.txt: /llms.txt per llmstxt.org: summary, current roles, page twins, PDFs, docs site, MCP server, contact, Optional. English, root only.
files.templates/md/llms-full.txt: /llms-full.txt: the whole CV as one markdown file. English.
files.templates/md/corpus/: The MCP corpus documents: profile.md, experience.md, role.md (one per role), education.md, courses.md, skills.md, contact.md. English; each opens with '# Title'.

assets.purpose: House style and behaviour, copied into dist/ byte for byte. site.css holds every design token and component; the JS is progressive enhancement only, so the site is complete without it. print.css is a separate stylesheet used only by templates/print/*.

files.assets/site.css: Every token (dark default, light theme override) and every component in docs/design-system.md. One stylesheet for the whole site.
files.assets/site.js: Progressive enhancement: reveal-on-scroll, nav solidify and mobile toggle, theme swap, count-up, typewriter, skill meters, timeline spine, command palette, cursor glow, scroll rail. All motion gated on prefers-reduced-motion.
files.assets/hero-net.js: The hero canvas (#hero-net): a small animated network graph, DPR-scaled to its parent, capped at about 34 nodes, paused when off-screen or the tab is hidden, one static frame under reduced motion.
files.assets/print.css: Print-only stylesheet: light ground, @page A4 with zero margin, a 210x297mm .sheet with its own 14mm padding, and the break-inside rules. No dark tokens, no animation.
files.assets/mark.svg: The personal mark used in the nav brand and the OG card.
files.assets/favicon.svg: The mark as an SVG. Deliberately not linked as an icon: browsers prefer an SVG icon over every PNG, which would override the portrait favicons.
files.assets/og/og-default.png: Generated 1200x630 social card, committed. Re-render it after editing templates/social/og.html.
files.assets/img/caleb.jpg: Portrait, with caleb-320.jpg as the small variant.
files.assets/favicon-32.png: Generated 32x32 icon, committed; also packed into favicon.ico.
files.assets/favicon-16.png: Generated 16x16 icon, committed; also packed into favicon.ico.
files.assets/icon-192.png: Generated 192x192 circular portrait: the favicon Google shows in results, the web manifest icon, and the docs site's favicon and header logo (copied into CalebSargeant/docs).
files.assets/icon-512.png: Generated 512x512 circular portrait for the web manifest.
files.assets/icon-maskable-512.png: Generated 512x512 square portrait, the manifest's maskable icon.
files.assets/site.webmanifest: Web app manifest: name, colours and the portrait icons. display is browser, so it is metadata, not an install prompt.

scripts.purpose: The build pipeline. build.py is the hub and the only place page metadata lives; render_pdf.py imports its PDFS list rather than keeping a copy. render_images.py is out of band, run by hand.

files.scripts/build.py: Loads data/*.yml, enriches roles (labels, durations, duties_see resolution, sorting), renders every entry in PAGES into dist/ plus a markdown twin of each sitemap page, copies assets and the root files, appends a canonical Link rule per twin to dist/_headers (failing past 100 rules), writes sitemap.xml, llms.txt and llms-full.txt, and writes the MCP corpus to .docs-index/index/website.json (schema 1, byte-identical for an unchanged build, anchors checked against the built pages). PAGES, PDFS and CORPUS are the page, document and corpus registries. Also serves dist/ with --serve.
files.scripts/render_pdf.py: Serves dist/ on an ephemeral localhost port and drives Playwright's Chromium to print the three sheets to dist/downloads/. Awaits document.fonts.ready, prints A4 with zero margins, warns past the MAX_PAGES budget. `--check` asserts the PDFs exist and are non-trivial.
files.scripts/render_images.py: Generates the committed images: the OG card from templates/social/og.html and the raster favicons, the manifest icons and favicon.ico, all face-cropped from assets/img/caleb.jpg. Run by hand, not by the build.

docs.purpose: The two contracts. Normative, not notes: a class name or a variable name here is the name in the CSS, the JS and the templates. Internal, never published to the site.

files.docs/design-system.md: Tokens, layout primitives, the exact class names / ids / data-attributes, the animation catalogue, the print rules, and the non-negotiable accessibility floor in section 6.
files.docs/template-context.md: Every variable build.py hands a template, the enriched role fields, the base.html block contract, and the templates/md/ contract (autoescape off, twin and corpus context, the shared macros).

config.purpose: Delivery and tooling config. The Worker is assets-only (no `main`), which is what keeps _headers authoritative. The crawl and disclosure surface sits at the repo root and is copied into dist/ verbatim.

files.wrangler.toml: The assets-only Worker: dist/ as the asset directory, 404-page not-found handling, workers_dev off with preview_urls explicitly on, and plain Workers routes for the apex and www. The apex is canonical; www is 301'd to it by a zone Redirect Rule that lives in Cloudflare, not here.
files._headers: CSP (third parties: Google Fonts, and the Cloudflare Web Analytics beacon the zone injects), HSTS, Permissions-Policy, cache policy and charset=utf-8 on .md and .txt. Authoritative only because the Worker has no code in the request path. build.py appends the per-page and per-twin Link rules in dist/.
files.Makefile: The front door: install, build, pdf, serve, clean. Everything real is in scripts/build.py.
files.requirements.txt: jinja2, pyyaml, playwright. Floors rather than pins, because none of it ships in the built site.
files.robots.txt: Content Signals, a Disallow on /print/ so the print sheets do not compete with the pages they mirror, the apex Sitemap line, and comments pointing assistants at llms.txt, llms-full.txt, the twins and the MCP server.
files..well-known/security.txt: RFC 9116 disclosure contact. Its Expires is hand-set; nothing stamps it.
files..well-known/ai-catalog.json: AI Catalog (Agent-Card/ai-catalog) listing the MCP server's card at mcp.calebsargeant.com/server-card, with ARD representativeQueries. Named by robots.txt's Agentmap line and the home pages' Link header.
files..well-known/api-catalog: RFC 9727 linkset pointing at the MCP server, its card (service-desc) and its guide page (service-doc). _headers sets its linkset+json media type.
files._redirects: One redirect: the legacy /.well-known/mcp/server-card.json probe to the card on the MCP host.
files.favicon.ico: Generated 16+32 icon at the repo root so /favicon.ico resolves. Committed.

ci.purpose: Deploy pipeline. Installs the Python deps and Chromium, builds the site and the PDFs, then publishes. Production on main, an aliased preview URL on a pull request.

files..github/workflows/deploy.yml: Push to main: build + PDFs, then `wrangler deploy`, then `wrangler r2 object put calebsargeant-docs-index/index/website.json ... --remote` to publish the MCP corpus (production only). Pull request: build + PDFs, then `wrangler versions upload` and the preview URL posted back on the PR. Needs CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID and CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN (with Workers R2 Storage: Edit for the publish), and Node 22 or newer for Wrangler.

callgraph_highlights.note: One pass: load the five YAML files, enrich roles, render every entry in PAGES and its markdown twin, copy assets and root files, append the twins' canonical Link rules to dist/_headers, write the sitemap, then llms.txt, llms-full.txt and the MCP corpus from the English context. dist/ is deleted first, so nothing survives a build that was not produced by it. --pdf shells out to render_pdf.py afterwards.
Prints what is already in dist/, it does not render templates. The document list is imported from build.py, so adding a fourth sheet to PAGES and PDFS is the only edit needed to get a fourth PDF.
Every site page extends base.html and links the one stylesheet and the one script. The print sheets deliberately do not: they are standalone documents linking assets/print.css only, with no JS.

The invariant this repo exists to hold: one fact, one place, four renderings. `highlights` feed the CV, `duties` feed the JDs PDF and the /experience details panel, `cover_letter` feeds the letter. Editing a rendering instead of the data is always the bug.
